title: Deadline-aware Autoscaler and Amortized Burst-Credit Smoothing
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a deadline-aware autoscaler that prioritizes latency-sensitive requests and a new amortized burst-credit smoothing mechanism to reduce eviction spikes and even out per-tenant credit burn. Adds telemetry for deadline miss rate and credit balance signals. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see oscillations when multiple tenants simultaneously consume burst credits to meet short deadlines. Current burst token pools are instantaneous and can cause sharp eviction fronts and SLA blips for tenants that require hard per-request deadlines. This PR implements two coordinated features: 1) a deadline-aware autoscaler that scores inflight and pending requests by a normalized deadline urgency and biases provisioning/slot allocation toward high-urgency work within safety bounds; 2) an amortized burst-credit smoothing algorithm that spreads burst consumption over a configurable window, converting instantaneous credit spikes into a controlled drain with cooldown and reclaimed buffers. The implementation is feature-flagged (feature.deadline_autoscale + feature.amortized_credit) and defaults to off for existing clusters. This PR also adds new telemetry (redwood_autoscaler_deadline_miss_rate, redwood_amortized_credit_burn_rate, redwood_credit_recovery_lag) and a calibration page in the Console. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-2045) - [x] unit tests for scoring and smoothing - [x] bazel integration tests - [x] e2e perf canary with synthetic deadline traffic - [x] docs update and migration notes - [x] feature flags and safe defaults
commits: 4 commits: 1) initial controller and scoring algorithm; 2) amortized-credit ledger and controller hooks; 3) telemetry + dashboards + tests; 4) docs and feature-flag wiring - commit msgs reference ENG-2045 and SUP-4421.
review_comments: Arjun: Asked for clearer invariants around guaranteed tenants vs best-effort; requested a hard cap to avoid starving low-priority tenants. Sofia: requested more unit tests around edge cases (zero-credit rollover and negative drift). Daniel: pointed out a potential race in ledger checkpointing under controller failover; asked for explicit lease renewal before writing checkpoint. Author responses: implemented per-tenant hard-minimum floor for guaranteed tenants, added ledger checkpoint backoff + lease renewal, expanded unit tests to cover negative drift and simultaneous reclaim. CI initially failed on a flaky perf integration test; rerun succeeded. Performance results: canary shows 22% reduction in 95th percentile deadline misses for mixed deadline/throughput traffic and 12% lower eviction spikes during sustained bursts.
notes_on_deployment: Feature gated rollout recommended: start with amortized_credit on a staging fleet, monitor redwood_amortized_credit_burn_rate and redwood_autoscaler_deadline_miss_rate for 24-72 hours; then enable deadline_autoscale on a subset of dedicated pools. Suggested config: amortized_window=300s, cooldown=120s, max_borrow_ratio=0.15. Added a command to console to simulate credits and throttling for tenants.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 42 new tests (autoscaler scoring, ledger invariants). Integration: perf canary against synthetic deadline workload (10k QPS, 20% deadline-sensitive). Observed metrics and stability thresholds logged in PR artifacts. Manual regression tests run for Dedicated upgrade path. Load test artifacts attached to Linear ticket ENG-2045.
docs_summary: Updated ops autoscaler doc with configuration examples, migration steps, and recommended thresholds. Added console dashboard and a runbook for troubleshooting deadline misses and credit starvation. Example configs placed under examples/perf-canary.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misconfiguration could privilege deadline traffic excessively and increase tail latency for best-effort tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant hard-min floors, global safety caps, feature flags, and staged rollout. Risk: new ledger writes under controller churn could cause brief credit double-counting; mitigation: lease-renewal + idempotent checkpoint writes and reconciliation job.
ui_changes: Console: new 'Deadline SLO' card on per-tenant page, credit burn heatmap, and a calibration panel for amortized_credit window. Dashboards added under observability/dashboards.
changelog_entry: Features: Deadline-aware autoscaling and amortized burst-credit smoothing (opt-in, dedicated fleets). Telemetry: redwood_autoscaler_deadline_miss_rate, redwood_amortized_credit_burn_rate.
migration_instructions: Clusters upgrading should keep feature flags off; operators can opt-in via helm values: feature.deadline_autoscale=true, feature.amortized_credit=true and set amortized_window/cooldown in values. Rolling update recommended with a single pool at a time.
